report: P0 Report Continuity Incident -- Forensic Dataset
methodology: Direct re-run of scripts/report_existence_validator.py logic against data/stix/feed_manifest.json and api/feed.json SEPARATELY on a fresh checkout of current main, superseding the stale pre-incident 546/1020 figures cited in the triggering CI run (#2140).

api/feed.json.note: Every report_url in this feed is fully-qualified/external (http-prefixed); report_existence_validator.py never checks these as local files, so this feed contributes 0 to STAGE 5.4.1 failures today.

pattern_observed: Missing entries are NOT concentrated in one catastrophic day -- they are spread across the last several days at a declining-but-nonzero rate (100% / 44.3% / 20.5% / 16.4% missing, oldest to newest day observed), consistent with an ONGOING per-run gap that partially self-corrects over subsequent runs, not a single historical incident.

root_cause_classification.primary_class: D -- Late-stage manifest rewrite/reconciliation without file-existence verification
root_cause_classification.description: scripts/generate_intel_reports.py (STAGE 3.6) is the sole engine that atomically writes a report HTML file, validates it (existence + min size + HTML signature), and ONLY THEN sets item["report_url"] -- on any failure it explicitly clears report_url to "". This engine never produces a dangling reference. However, scripts/run_pipeline.py stage_sync_root_feed_json() runs a SECOND time at the very end of the pipeline (after STAGE 3.6) and performs a canonical manifest write-back (Step 7) that includes a RECONCILIATION sub-step: items present in the quality-engine-filtered payload but not matched by id/stix_id in the pre-quality manifest snapshot are APPENDED verbatim -- report_url field included -- with no re-check that the file it names exists in this run's working tree. Any upstream mechanism that carries an item (and its report_url) forward across runs without going through STAGE 3.6's own generation for THIS run (the intel_quality_engine's own source-balancing/carry-forward behavior, or the prev_feed thin-manifest fallback) can introduce exactly this class of dangling reference.
root_cause_classification.secondary_contributing_factor: scripts/safe_git_commit.py (STAGE 4) confirmed actively exercising a conflict-recovery cascade in production (8 "conflict-recovery" commits found in the last 300 commits on main, including one from ~2 hours before this investigation) that restores both reports/ (as a directory union via ) and data/stix/feed_manifest.json (as a full single-file replace via the same ref) from ORIG_HEAD independently. This composition is SAFE as long as ORIG_HEAD itself is materialization-clean (a directory-union restore can only add files, never remove the ones a clean manifest references) -- meaning this cascade amplifies/propagates an upstream gap rather than independently causing one. Fixing the true final-writer gap (Step 7's reconciliation) is therefore sufficient; safe_git_commit.py required no changes.
root_cause_classification.unrelated_finding_not_in_scope: data/stix/feed_manifest.json on committed main (verified via ) is currently a bare JSON list, not the {"advisories": [...]} dict envelope that stage_sync_root_feed_json() Step 7 (v143.1.1) intends to always produce -- meaning Step 7 is silently failing or being bypassed on some runs. This is a real, separate format-integrity question worth its own investigation, but is NOT the cause of the report_url/file dangling-reference defect (reproduced and fixed identically regardless of which envelope shape the manifest was in) and is explicitly left untouched here per the minimal-change-surface mandate. The new materialization barrier defensively re-envelopes to dict before its own repair pass runs, purely to guarantee it can never itself narrow the manifest -- it does not address why the drift happens upstream.
